This is a completely untenable policy. In one short-sighted move, Reddit has assumed responsibility for all the content posted on its site and all the offense people take therein. It used to be that if a person encountered offensive speech, they directed their anger at the user who posted it. Now they can legitimately direct their anger at Reddit itself.

Just to be clear, this means Reddit has angered both the people they have censored AND the SJWs who think Reddit haven't gone far enough. The mods of the banned subreddits are pissed. Free speech advocates are pissed. SJWs are pissed. I have no idea how Reddit intends to grow if they have angered their entire user base.

And ultimately, this is all about trust. The most important trait for any source of information is that the consumer can trust it; can trust that they are not being denied access to certain info behind the scenes; can trust censors are not preventing users from learning "undesirable" things.

Seeing the way Reddit began shadowbanning users, began deleting posts about Voat, and has declared itself the authority on what is and is not 'abhorrent', I have lost all trust I had in Reddit.
